events.title: Pepin the Short dies, leaving the Franks to Charlemagne and Carloman
events.description: King Pepin died at Saint-Denis, dividing his kingdom between his sons Charles and Carloman, who were crowned in October. After Carloman's death in 771, Charlemagne ruled alone.
events.html: King Pepin died at Saint-Denis, dividing his kingdom between his sons Charles and Carloman, who were crowned in October. After Carloman's death in 771, Charlemagne ruled alone.

events.title: Washington signs the Judiciary Act
events.description: The Judiciary Act set up the federal court system, fixed the Supreme Court at six justices and created the office of Attorney General. It remains the foundation of the US federal judiciary.
events.html: The Judiciary Act set up the federal court system, fixed the Supreme Court at six justices and created the office of Attorney General. It remains the foundation of the US federal judiciary.

events.title: Gold price collapses on 'Black Friday'
events.description: Jay Gould and James Fisk's attempt to corner the gold market collapsed when the Grant administration sold Treasury gold. Prices crashed and many speculators were ruined.
events.html: Jay Gould and James Fisk's attempt to corner the gold market collapsed when the Grant administration sold Treasury gold. Prices crashed and many speculators were ruined.

events.title: B. R. Ambedkar and Hindu leaders sign the Poona Pact
events.description: Agreed with Gandhi during his fast, the Poona Pact was signed, replacing separate electorates for the 'depressed classes' with reserved seats. Gandhi ended his fast against separate electorates two days later.

events.title: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty opens for signature
events.description: The CTBT, banning all nuclear explosions, opened for signature at the UN and was signed first by President Clinton. It has not entered into force, as key states have not ratified it.
